_meta.description: Curated offline subset of the MITRE ATT&CK Enterprise matrix used for local technique mapping. Not a complete copy of ATT&CK.
_meta.license_note: MITRE ATT&CK is a registered trademark of The MITRE Corporation. Content is summarised here for offline demonstration under the ATT&CK Terms of Use.

techniques.name: Phishing
techniques.description: Adversaries send phishing messages to gain access to victim systems, typically with malicious attachments or links.
techniques.detection: Inspect email gateway logs for anomalous senders, newly registered domains and attachment types not typical for the organisation.

techniques.name: Phishing: Spearphishing Attachment
techniques.description: Adversaries send targeted emails containing malicious attachments to execute code on victim systems.
techniques.detection: Alert on Office applications spawning script interpreters shortly after an email delivery event.
mitigations: Disable Office macros from the internet

techniques.name: Phishing: Spearphishing Link
techniques.description: Adversaries send targeted emails containing links to credential-harvesting or malware-delivery sites.
techniques.detection: Correlate proxy logs against newly registered or low-reputation domains referenced in inbound mail.

techniques.name: Valid Accounts
techniques.tactic: Defense Evasion, Persistence, Privilege Escalation, Initial Access
techniques.description: Adversaries obtain and abuse credentials of existing accounts to blend in with legitimate activity.
techniques.detection: Baseline per-user logon geography, device and time-of-day; alert on deviations and on service accounts logging in interactively.

techniques.name: Brute Force
techniques.description: Adversaries systematically guess credentials to gain account access.
techniques.detection: Threshold and velocity rules on failed authentication events per source IP and per account.

techniques.name: Brute Force: Password Spraying
techniques.description: Adversaries try a small number of common passwords against many accounts to avoid lockouts.
techniques.detection: Alert on a single source authenticating against an unusually high number of distinct accounts.

techniques.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
techniques.description: Adversaries abuse command and script interpreters to execute commands, scripts or binaries.
techniques.detection: Monitor process creation events for interpreters spawned by unusual parents.

techniques.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: PowerShell
techniques.description: Adversaries abuse PowerShell to execute commands and payloads, frequently with encoded arguments.
techniques.detection: Enable script block logging; alert on -EncodedCommand, -ExecutionPolicy Bypass and hidden window styles.

techniques.name: Scheduled Task/Job: Scheduled Task
techniques.description: Adversaries create scheduled tasks to execute payloads on a schedule or at startup.
techniques.detection: Monitor 4698 task-creation events and schtasks.exe command lines referencing user-writable paths.

techniques.name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Registry Run Keys
techniques.description: Adversaries add programs to registry run keys so they execute when a user logs on.
techniques.detection: Alert on writes to Run/RunOnce keys referencing executables in temp or user profile directories.

techniques.name: OS Credential Dumping
techniques.description: Adversaries dump credential material from the operating system to enable lateral movement.
techniques.detection: Alert on handle access to lsass.exe by non-standard processes and on ntds.dit copies.

techniques.name: OS Credential Dumping: LSASS Memory
techniques.description: Adversaries access LSASS process memory to extract credentials.
techniques.detection: EDR rules on cross-process handle requests to lsass.exe with read-memory rights.

techniques.name: Remote Services
techniques.description: Adversaries use valid accounts to log into remote services and move laterally.
techniques.detection: Correlate authentication events across hosts for the same account in short time windows.

techniques.name: Remote Services: Remote Desktop Protocol
techniques.description: Adversaries use RDP to log into and control remote systems.
techniques.detection: Alert on RDP logons from workstations to servers and on internet-exposed 3389.

techniques.name: Remote Services: SMB/Windows Admin Shares
techniques.description: Adversaries use SMB admin shares (C$, ADMIN$) to move laterally and stage payloads.
techniques.detection: Monitor 5140/5145 share access events for administrative shares from non-admin hosts.

techniques.name: Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols
techniques.description: Adversaries communicate with C2 infrastructure over HTTP/S to blend with normal traffic.
techniques.detection: Detect periodic beaconing (low jitter), rare user-agents and long-lived connections to new domains.

techniques.name: Application Layer Protocol: DNS
techniques.description: Adversaries use DNS queries for C2 communication or data transfer.
techniques.detection: Alert on high-entropy or unusually long subdomains and high query volume to a single domain.

techniques.name: Ingress Tool Transfer
techniques.description: Adversaries transfer tools or files from an external system into a compromised environment.
techniques.detection: Monitor for LOLBins performing network downloads to user-writable paths.

techniques.name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
techniques.description: Adversaries steal data by exfiltrating it over an existing command and control channel.
techniques.detection: Baseline per-host outbound byte volume; alert on statistical outliers to rare destinations.

techniques.name: Exfiltration Over Web Service: Cloud Storage
techniques.description: Adversaries exfiltrate data to cloud storage services to blend with legitimate traffic.
techniques.detection: Alert on unusual upload volume to consumer file-sharing services from server subnets.

techniques.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
techniques.description: Adversaries encrypt data on target systems to interrupt availability, i.e. ransomware.
techniques.detection: Detect rapid mass file modification, shadow copy deletion and ransom-note creation.

techniques.name: Inhibit System Recovery
techniques.description: Adversaries delete backups and shadow copies to prevent recovery.
techniques.detection: Alert on vssadmin delete shadows, wbadmin delete catalog and bcdedit recovery changes.

techniques.name: Process Injection
techniques.description: Adversaries inject code into live processes to evade defences and elevate privileges.
techniques.detection: EDR telemetry on cross-process memory writes and remote thread creation.

techniques.name: Modify Registry
techniques.description: Adversaries modify the registry to hide configuration, disable security tooling or persist.
techniques.detection: Audit changes to security-product and policy registry keys.

techniques.name: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools
techniques.description: Adversaries disable security tooling to avoid detection.
techniques.detection: Alert on security service stops, AV exclusion additions and agent uninstall events.

techniques.name: Create Account: Local Account
techniques.description: Adversaries create local accounts to maintain access.
techniques.detection: Alert on 4720/4732 events outside change windows, especially additions to local administrators.

techniques.name: Account Discovery
techniques.description: Adversaries enumerate accounts to understand the environment and plan movement.
techniques.detection: Alert on discovery command bursts from a single host or user session.

techniques.name: Remote System Discovery
techniques.description: Adversaries enumerate remote hosts to identify lateral movement targets.
techniques.detection: Detect scanning behaviour: many distinct destination IPs or ports from one internal source.

techniques.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
techniques.description: Adversaries exploit internet-facing applications to gain initial access.
techniques.detection: WAF alerts correlated with anomalous child processes from web server accounts.

techniques.name: Account Manipulation
techniques.description: Adversaries modify accounts (roles, credentials, MFA devices) to maintain or elevate access.
techniques.detection: Alert on privileged role assignments and MFA method registrations outside normal workflows.
